```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.path = "figures/")
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw())
sci <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 0)   # 1e-08 instead of 0.000
```

# 1. Aim

The oxygen screening solver was run on the real leaf for every combination of:

- `P_wall`: how easily oxygen crosses the vessel wall (m/s), 4 levels.
- `Vmax`: how fast the tissue consumes oxygen (mM/s), 3 levels.
- `inlet_mmHg`: oxygen entering the network (mmHg), 2 levels.

The leaf geometry was rebuilt from the saved NetFlowV2 network, because the
original LeafVeinCNN file was lost (`src/reconstruct/network_to_mat.py`). All
other settings are the May settings.

Questions:

1. Is every run physically possible?
2. Does the rebuilt leaf give the same answers as the May sweep report?
3. Which parameter controls tissue oxygen most?
4. What did the wall-exchange fix change on the real leaf?

# 2. Load and check

```{r load}
sweep <- read_csv(params$sweep)
cat("Runs:", nrow(sweep), "\n")
sweep %>% count(P_wall_m_s, name = "runs") %>%
  mutate(P_wall_m_s = sci(P_wall_m_s)) %>% knitr::kable()
```

Tissue has no oxygen source other than the vessels, so tissue pO2 should never
be above the inlet value.

```{r checks}
checks <- sweep %>% summarise(
  runs = n(),
  missing_values = sum(is.na(tissue_pO2_median_mmHg)),
  tissue_above_inlet = sum(tissue_pO2_max_mmHg > inlet_mmHg + 0.5),
  flagged_by_solver = sum(nonphysical_tissue_gt_inlet))
knitr::kable(checks)
```

# 3. Comparison with the May sweep report

The May sweep table was lost, but the May report still shows the percentage of
tissue at or above 15 mmHg for its 12 runs, and two group medians. The same 12
conditions are inside the new sweep.

```{r may-compare}
may <- read_csv(params$may_report, comment = "#")

frac <- may %>% filter(quantity == "frac_tissue_ge_15mmHg_pct") %>%
  mutate(across(c(P_wall_m_s, Vmax_mM_s, inlet_mmHg), as.numeric)) %>%
  select(P_wall_m_s, Vmax_mM_s, inlet_mmHg, may_report = value) %>%
  inner_join(sweep %>% select(P_wall_m_s, Vmax_mM_s, inlet_mmHg,
                              rebuilt_leaf = frac_tissue_ge_15mmHg_pct),
             by = c("P_wall_m_s", "Vmax_mM_s", "inlet_mmHg")) %>%
  mutate(difference = rebuilt_leaf - may_report)

knitr::kable(frac %>% mutate(P_wall_m_s = sci(P_wall_m_s), Vmax_mM_s = sci(Vmax_mM_s)),
             digits = 1, caption = "Tissue >= 15 mmHg (%)")
```

```{r may-medians}
group_medians <- sweep %>%
  filter(P_wall_m_s %in% c(1e-8, 1e-6)) %>%
  group_by(P_wall_m_s) %>%
  summarise(rebuilt_leaf = median(tissue_pO2_median_mmHg)) %>%
  mutate(may_report = c(4.02, 104))
knitr::kable(group_medians %>% mutate(P_wall_m_s = sci(P_wall_m_s)), digits = 2,
             caption = "Median of the run medians of tissue pO2 (mmHg), 6 runs per P_wall")
```

```{r may-summary, include = FALSE}
lo <- frac %>% filter(P_wall_m_s == 1e-8)
hi <- frac %>% filter(P_wall_m_s == 1e-6)
worst <- frac %>% slice_max(abs(difference), n = 1)
```

The regime result is the same. At `P_wall` = 1e-8, `r if (max(lo$rebuilt_leaf) < 0.05) "no tissue reaches 15 mmHg in any condition" else paste0("at most ", round(max(lo$rebuilt_leaf), 1), "% of tissue reaches 15 mmHg")`
(May report: at most `r max(lo$may_report)`%). At 1e-6, at least
`r round(min(hi$rebuilt_leaf), 1)`% does (May report: at least
`r min(hi$may_report)`%). The largest difference is
`r round(abs(worst$difference), 1)` percentage points, at `Vmax` =
`r sci(worst$Vmax_mM_s)` and inlet `r worst$inlet_mmHg` mmHg, the condition
with the highest consumption and the lowest supply.

The rebuilt leaf gives less oxygen than the May report: the group medians are
`r round(group_medians$rebuilt_leaf[1], 1)` vs 4.02 mmHg and
`r round(group_medians$rebuilt_leaf[2], 1)` vs 104 mmHg. The likely reason is
geometry. The rebuilt veins are straight segments between nodes, with the
NetFlowV2 diameters (capped at 150 µm), not the original CNN outline, so vein
area and spacing differ. The rebuilt leaf therefore reproduces the May
conclusions, not the May numbers.

# 4. Effect of each parameter

```{r median-po2, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(sweep, aes(P_wall_m_s, tissue_pO2_median_mmHg,
                  colour = sci(Vmax_mM_s), group = Vmax_mM_s)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = inlet_mmHg), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 15, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("Inlet", inlet_mmHg, "mmHg")) +
  labs(x = "P_wall (m/s, log scale)", y = "Median tissue pO2 (mmHg)",
       colour = "Vmax (mM/s)",
       title = "Real leaf: median tissue oxygen",
       subtitle = "dashed = inlet pO2, dotted = 15 mmHg")
```

To compare the parameters fairly, tissue pO2 is divided by the inlet pO2. For
each parameter, the mean of this ratio is taken at each of its levels
(averaging over the other two). The spread between its lowest and highest level
is its main effect.

```{r main-effects}
sweep <- sweep %>% mutate(ratio = tissue_pO2_median_mmHg / inlet_mmHg)
main_effect <- function(df, var) {
  df %>% group_by(level = .data[[var]]) %>%
    summarise(mean_ratio = mean(ratio), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(parameter = var)
}
effects <- bind_rows(main_effect(sweep, "P_wall_m_s"),
                     main_effect(sweep, "Vmax_mM_s"),
                     main_effect(sweep, "inlet_mmHg"))
knitr::kable(effects %>% transmute(parameter,
                                   level = ifelse(parameter == "inlet_mmHg", format(level), sci(level)),
                                   mean_ratio), digits = 3)
spread <- effects %>% group_by(parameter) %>%
  summarise(spread = max(mean_ratio) - min(mean_ratio)) %>% arrange(desc(spread))
knitr::kable(spread, digits = 3)
```

`r spread$parameter[1]` has the largest effect (spread
`r round(spread$spread[1], 2)`), then `r spread$parameter[2]`
(`r round(spread$spread[2], 2)`), then `r spread$parameter[3]`
(`r round(spread$spread[3], 2)`). The tested ranges are not evenly spaced, so
this ranks the parameters over the ranges tested, not per unit change.

# 5. The wall-exchange fix on the real leaf

The May solver updated wall exchange explicitly, in the same step as diffusion.
When `dt * k` was large, the update overshot and tissue oxygen went above the
inlet. The current solver treats exchange semi-implicitly
(`src/solver/oxy_sim_mat.py`, `compute_step`).

The runs at `P_wall` = 1e-6 and 1e-4 were repeated with the May solver.

```{r fix}
before <- read_csv(params$before_fix) %>%
  select(run_id, P_wall_m_s, Vmax_mM_s, inlet_mmHg,
         median_before = tissue_pO2_median_mmHg, max_before = tissue_pO2_max_mmHg)
fix <- before %>%
  inner_join(sweep %>% select(run_id, median_after = tissue_pO2_median_mmHg,
                              max_after = tissue_pO2_max_mmHg), by = "run_id") %>%
  mutate(above_inlet_before = max_before > inlet_mmHg + 0.5,
         above_inlet_after = max_after > inlet_mmHg + 0.5)
fix_table <- fix %>% group_by(P_wall_m_s) %>%
  summarise(runs = n(),
            max_change_in_median_mmHg = max(abs(median_after - median_before)),
            highest_median_before = max(median_before),
            highest_max_before = max(max_before),
            runs_above_inlet_before = sum(above_inlet_before),
            runs_above_inlet_after = sum(above_inlet_after))
knitr::kable(fix_table %>% mutate(P_wall_m_s = sci(P_wall_m_s)), digits = 2)
```

```{r fix-plot, fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot(fix, aes(median_before, median_after, colour = sci(P_wall_m_s),
                shape = factor(inlet_mmHg))) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Median tissue pO2, May solver (mmHg)", y = "Fixed solver (mmHg)",
       colour = "P_wall (m/s)", shape = "Inlet (mmHg)")
```

```{r fix-summary, include = FALSE}
f6 <- fix_table %>% filter(P_wall_m_s == 1e-6)
f4 <- fix_table %>% filter(P_wall_m_s == 1e-4)
```

At `P_wall` = 1e-6, the highest level in the May report, the fix changes the
median tissue pO2 by at most `r signif(f6$max_change_in_median_mmHg, 2)` mmHg,
so the May report's conclusions stand. At 1e-4, the May solver puts tissue
oxygen above the inlet in `r f4$runs_above_inlet_before` of `r f4$runs` runs,
with a maximum of `r round(f4$highest_max_before)` mmHg, which is physically
impossible. The fixed solver does so in `r f4$runs_above_inlet_after` runs.

# 6. What this does and does not show

- The solver gives bounded, consistent answers on the real leaf geometry, and
  the rebuilt leaf reproduces the May sweep conclusions.
- Wall permeability decides whether the tissue is oxygenated. It has not been
  measured for decellularised leaves, so the answer is conditional on it.
- No result here is a measurement or a viability prediction. There is no
  experimental comparison.
- The solver builds its own flow field on the vein skeleton, with one inlet and
  one outlet. It does not use the NetFlowV2 flows from the outlet study.
